abstract: The nephron is a highly compartmentalized structure, where distinct patterns of somatic mosaicism may be established and contribute to altered kidney functions with aging. Here we show extensive remodeling of aged nephrons by mosaic clones using integrated sequencing of >1,000 microdissected samples collected from anatomically distinct nephron segments. Striking differences were observed across segments. Proximal tubules exhibited markedly higher mutation burdens with mutational signatures characteristic of clear cell renal cell carcinoma and larger clonal expansion than other segments. Cancer-related mutations were observed only infrequently and largely limited to proximal tubules, while copy number abnormalities were quite common, most frequently involving chromosomes 18, 10, 7, X, 22, 3 and 9, in a segment-specific manner. Clone size appears to depend more on cell turnover than on driver events. Particularly, in collecting ducts, numerous clones independently acquiring chromosome 18 loss evolved over years and ultimately replaced 15-47% of collecting duct cells in aged donors despite minimal increase in their clone size, likely reflecting strong fitness advantage of chromosome 18-deficient clones under slow tissue turnover. Chromosome 18-deficient cells significantly correlated with fibrosis and showed reduced expression of chromosome 18 genes, including those involved in sodium handling (NEDD4L) and TGF-{beta} signaling (SMAD2/4/7). In line with this, GSEA of chromosome 18-deficient cells revealed enhanced hallmark pathways overlapping those associated with acute kidney injury that are related to TGF-{beta} signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and inflammatory responses. These findings illustrate how nephrons are remodeled with aging, providing insights into the role of somatic remodelling in altered kidney structures and functions with aging.
